newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to allow import of Vietnamese labour.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to allow import of Vietnamese labour.

text.p: Taiwan will allow Vietnamese nationals to work on the island in 1997, the vice chairman of the Council for Labour Affairs said on Wednesday.

"We have decided to allow local companies to recruit workers from Vietnam, but this does not mean we will increase the number of foreign nationals working in Taiwan," vice chairman Chan Ho-sheng told Reuters by telephone.

"We only increase the choices of the countries from which Taiwan's employers can recruit prospective workers," he said, denying local press reports that the council had decided to increase the quota for the imported workers.
Taiwan permits local firms to import a total of 292,000 workers from Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Thailand. To date, 250,000 have been recruited.
Chan said employers now can choose from among the five countries once Vietnam is included in the near future.

He said there was no limit on how many Vietnamese workers could be employed, but said if more companies employ workers from that country it would force a corresponding cut in the number of workers imported from the other four countries.
He said as soon as the foreign ministry signed a labour cooperation memorandum with Vietnam, importation of Vietnamese workers was likely to begin in 1997.

Thailand is the biggest supplier of workers to Taiwan, accounting for more than 60 percent of the 250,000-strong foreign work force, followed by the Philippines at 30 percent. The rest come from Malaysia and Thailand.
Workers are allowed to work no more than two years and must return home after their contracts expire.
